entry: Body of myths of the North Germanic peoples of Scandinavia, preserved mainly in medieval Icelandic manuscripts. Its principal sources are the anonymous *Poetic Edda* and the *Prose Edda* of [[Snorri Sturluson]], both recorded in the 13th century, along with sagas and archaeological evidence. The cosmos comprises Nine Worlds linked by the world tree [[Yggdrasil]]. The most prominent gods include [[Odin]], god of wisdom, poetry and war; [[Thor]], wielder of the hammer Mjölnir; and [[Freyja]], goddess of love and beauty. The shape-shifting trickster [[Loki]] causes conflict among the gods. The myths culminate in Ragnarök, a battle in which most gods and the world perish, after which a renewed earth emerges. Scholars have studied the myths since the 17th century, and adherents of Germanic Neopaganism revive them in a religious context.

Northern portion of the African continent. The most common definition includes Algeria, Egypt, Libya, Morocco, Tunisia and Western Sahara, the territory disputed between Morocco and the Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic; the United Nations also includes Sudan. The [[Sahara]] covers much of the region, the [[Atlas Mountains]] rise in the northwest, and the [[Nile]] supports Egypt's population. [[Berbers]] have lived in the northwest since the beginning of recorded history. Arab conquests of the seventh and eighth centuries brought [[Islam]] and Arabization, and Arabs now form the majority in every North African country. The region is associated with the [[Middle East]] in geopolitics. The 2011 [[Arab Spring]] protests toppled leaders in Tunisia, Egypt and Libya, with mixed outcomes.

American long-range fighter and fighter-bomber used in [[World War II]] and the [[Korean War]]. Designed by North American Aviation at British request, it first flew on October 26, 1940. A Rolls-Royce Merlin engine, licensed by Packard as the V-1650, greatly improved high-altitude performance. The P-51D, with a bubble canopy and six .50-caliber machine guns, escorted bombers over Germany from 1943 to 1945. Mustang pilots claimed 4,950 enemy aircraft in World War II. Redesignated F-51 for the Korean War, it was superseded by jet fighters but remained in some air forces until the early 1980s.

State in the southeastern United States, one of the [[Thirteen Colonies]] (pop., 2020: 10,439,388). Raleigh is the capital, and Charlotte is the largest city. The Halifax Resolves of April 12, 1776, were the first formal call for independence from Great Britain among the colonies. The state ratified the U.S. Constitution on November 21, 1789, as the 12th state. It seceded in 1861 to join the [[Confederate States of America]] and was restored to the Union in 1868. On December 17, 1903, the [[Wright brothers]] made the world's first controlled, sustained powered flight at Kitty Hawk, in the Outer Banks.

Largest alluvial plain of China, in the north of the country. Formed in a downfaulted rift basin during the late [[Paleogene]] and [[Neogene]] and later built up by Yellow River deposits, it covers about 409,500 sq km (158,100 sq mi), mostly under 50 meters (160 ft) above sea level. It is bordered by the Yanshan, Taihang and Dabie mountains. Its fertile soils produce wheat, maize, sorghum, millet, peanuts, cotton and vegetables, and it is one of the most densely populated regions in the world. The Central Plain along the middle and lower [[Yellow River]] was the cradle of Chinese civilization and the region from which the [[Han Chinese]] emerged. [[Beijing]], the national capital, lies on its northeast edge. Floods and droughts are both common, and many historians argue that the plain's flat geography encouraged a centralized state to manage granaries, waterworks and fortifications against steppe peoples, prompting construction of the [[Great Wall of China]].

Landlocked U.S. state in the Upper Midwest, part of the [[Great Plains]] (pop., 2025: 799,358). Bismarck is the capital, and Fargo is the largest city. The Mandan, Hidatsa and Arikara lived along the [[Missouri River]], while [[Ojibwe]], Cree and [[Sioux]] peoples lived elsewhere. It was admitted to the Union on November 2, 1889, as the 39th state. Wheat farming replaced the fur trade. Since the early 2000s, oil from the Bakken formation has driven much of the state's prosperity. The Bank of North Dakota is the nation's only state-run bank.

One of the two main islands of [[New Zealand]], separated from the larger but less populous [[South Island]] by [[Cook Strait]]. It covers 113,729 sq km (43,911 sq mi), making it the world's 14th-largest island and 43% of New Zealand's land area. Its population of 4,067,400 (June 2025) is 76% of the national total, and it is the most populous island in Polynesia. Its official Māori name, Te Ika-a-Māui ("the fish of Māui"), refers to a myth in which the demigod Māui pulled the island from the sea. [[Auckland]], the largest city, lies in the north, and [[Wellington]], the capital, is at the southwestern tip. The central volcanic zone contains Lake Taupō, New Zealand's largest lake.

Country occupying the northern half of the Korean Peninsula, officially the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK). A Soviet-aligned government was established in the north in 1948, and the [[Korean War]] began with its invasion of South Korea in 1950. The 1953 armistice created the demilitarized zone. [[Kim Il Sung]], the first leader, promoted the state ideology of [[Juche]]. After the [[Soviet Union]] dissolved in 1991, the economy declined sharply. North Korea suffered a famine from 1994 to 1998, and malnutrition has continued. In 2024 it abandoned efforts to reunify Korea and designated South Korea a hostile state. Its government, led by the [[Workers' Party of Korea]], has been described as a totalitarian hereditary dictatorship centered on the Kim family. Amnesty International considers its human rights record the worst in the world. The country has nuclear weapons, and its army of 1.28 million is the fourth largest in the world. It has been a [[United Nations]] member since 1991.

Landlocked country in southeastern Europe, officially the Republic of North Macedonia. Its capital, [[Skopje]], is home to about a quarter of the population of more than 1.83 million. Most residents are ethnic Macedonians, a South Slavic people, and Albanians form a significant minority of around 25%. In classical antiquity the region was subjugated by the Persian Empire, incorporated into the kingdom of Macedonia, and later conquered by Rome. It came under [[Ottoman Empire]] rule in the late 14th century and passed to Serbian rule after the [[Balkan Wars]] of 1912–1913. It became a constituent state of communist [[Yugoslavia]] in 1945 and declared independence in 1991. It joined the United Nations in 1993. In 2019 it adopted the prefix "North" in its name, resolving a dispute with [[Greece]], and its accession to [[NATO|North Atlantic Treaty Organization]] followed in 2020. It has been a candidate for [[European Union]] membership since 2005.

Northernmost point on Earth, at 90° North latitude, where the planet's axis of rotation meets the surface. It is also called the True North Pole to distinguish it from the magnetic north pole. The Pole lies in the middle of the [[Arctic Ocean]], on constantly shifting sea ice rather than on land as the [[South Pole]] does. The nearest land is Kaffeklubben Island, about 700 km (430 mi) away off northern [[Greenland]]. Sea depths of more than 4,000 meters (13,100 feet) make a permanent station impractical, although Soviet and later Russian drifting stations have passed close to the Pole. Earlier claims by Frederick Cook, Robert Peary and Richard Byrd were later doubted. The first undisputed expedition to reach it was the airship *Norge*, which overflew the area in 1926 under [[Roald Amundsen]]. The first complete land expedition arrived in 1968, using snowmobiles and air support.

Landlocked state in western [[Germany]], the most populous German state, with more than 18 million inhabitants. [[Düsseldorf]] is the capital, and [[Cologne]], with over one million residents, is the largest city. The state was established in 1946 by the British military administration from the Prussian provinces of Westphalia and the northern Rhine Province, and it joined the Federal Republic in 1949. [[Bonn]] was the federal capital until reunification in 1990 and the seat of government until 1999. Its economy is the largest of the German states by gross regional product.

Shallow sea of the [[Atlantic Ocean]] on the European continental shelf, lying between [[Great Britain]] and northern continental Europe. It is more than 970 km (600 mi) long and 580 km (360 mi) wide, with a mean depth of 90 meters (300 ft). It connects to the Atlantic through the [[English Channel]] in the south and to the Norwegian Sea in the north. The sea was central to the rise of the Vikings, and the [[Hanseatic League]], the Dutch Republic and Britain all sought command of it. As Germany's only outlet to the ocean, it was strategically important in both world wars. The sea supports major shipping lanes and fisheries, and offshore oil, gas and wind energy are now significant. Overfishing, industrial and agricultural runoff, and dumping have prompted efforts to protect its ecosystems.

Island of the [[Andaman and Nicobar Islands]] in the [[Bay of Bengal]], a protected area of India. It is home to the [[Sentinelese]], an uncontacted indigenous people who have often defended their isolation with violence. A 1956 regulation prohibits travel to the island and any approach within five kilometers (three miles). The Indian Navy patrols the area, and the government does not prosecute the Sentinelese for killing outsiders who land. In 2006 islanders killed two fishermen whose boat drifted ashore. In 2018 the American missionary John Allen Chau was killed after he illegally tried to contact them.

1959 American thriller film directed by [[Alfred Hitchcock]], starring [[Cary Grant]], [[Eva Marie Saint]] and James Mason. Advertising executive Roger Thornhill is mistaken for a nonexistent government agent, George Kaplan, and pursued across the United States by agents of a mysterious organization smuggling microfilm. The story culminates in an action sequence on [[Mount Rushmore]]. Its opening credits, designed by Saul Bass, were the first to feature extended kinetic typography. The film topped the U.S. box office for seven consecutive weeks and received three [[Academy Awards]] nominations. In 1995 the [[Library of Congress]] selected it for the National Film Registry.

Largest national park in the world, covering the interior and northeastern coast of [[Greenland]]. Established in 1974 and expanded to 972,000 sq km (375,000 sq mi) in 1988, it is bigger than 166 of the world's 195 countries. It is the northernmost national park in the world and the first created in the Kingdom of Denmark. The park has no permanent population. In 2008 about 31 people wintered at stations, including a patrol headquarters and a military base, with about 110 dogs. Much of the interior lies under the [[Greenland ice sheet]]. Its coasts support an estimated 5,000 to 15,000 musk oxen, along with [[Polar bear|polar bears]], [[Walrus|walruses]], [[Narwhal|narwhals]] and [[Beluga whale|beluga whales]].

Easternmost region of [[India]], officially the North Eastern Region (NER), covering 262,184 sq km (101,230 sq mi), or about 8% of India's area. It comprises the states of Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland and Tripura, known as the "Seven Sisters," along with Sikkim. The region is one of the most linguistically diverse in the world and borders [[China]], [[Myanmar]], Bangladesh, Nepal and [[Bhutan]]. A corridor of land known as the Siliguri Corridor connects it to the rest of India. India's first oil well was dug at Digboi in Assam in 1865. The Battle of Imphal and Kohima in 1944 was fought in the region during World War II. Many people of Mizoram, Meghalaya and Nagaland converted to [[Christianity]] under British missionaries during the [[British Raj]]. The North Eastern Council, established in 1971, coordinates development.

One of the four regions defined by the U.S. Census Bureau, on the Atlantic coast. It comprises the six [[New England]] states and New Jersey, New York and Pennsylvania. It is the most densely populated U.S. region, with 320 people per square mile, and the smallest by total area. Its population of 57,609,148 is concentrated in the Northeast megalopolis, which includes [[New York City]], [[Philadelphia]] and [[Boston]]. All of its states were among the original [[Thirteen Colonies]], although Maine and Vermont belonged to other colonies until independence. The region's gross domestic product was $5.1 trillion in 2022.

Military campaigns by Catholic kingdoms and military orders to Christianize the pagan peoples around the southern and eastern shores of the [[Baltic Sea]]. The most notable were the Prussian and Livonian Crusades, the latter of which also fought the Orthodox states of [[Novgorod Republic]] and Pskov. Some campaigns, such as the Wendish Crusade of 1147 against the Slavs between the Elbe and Oder rivers, were partly aimed at controlling rich resources. The official starting point was a call by [[Pope]] Celestine III in 1195. The German [[Teutonic Order]] spearheaded many incursions and profited from them. Lithuania maintained paganism until its ruler's voluntary conversion in 1387, marking the effective end of crusading against the Baltic pagans. The campaigns extended Western feudal institutions and church authority into northeastern Europe.

De facto state occupying the northern third of the island of [[Cyprus]], officially the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus (TRNC). Only [[Turkey]] recognizes it; the international community regards it as territory of the Republic of Cyprus under Turkish military occupation. Turkey invaded in 1974, after a coup by the Greek military junta aimed at annexing the island, and the northern area declared independence in 1983. United Nations Security Council Resolution 541 rejected the declaration as legally invalid. The entity depends on Turkey for economic, political and military support. Some experts call it a puppet state of Turkey, while others dispute the label. Its official language is Turkish, and its economy is dominated by services.

Half of Earth that lies north of the [[Equator]]. Because of Earth's axial tilt of 23.439281°, the hemisphere has seasonal variation in day length and temperature. Winter is conventionally counted from the December solstice to the March equinox, and summer from the June solstice to the September equinox. Its surface is 60.7% water, and it contains 67.3% of Earth's land. North America and mainland [[Eurasia]] lie entirely within it. Inside the [[Arctic Circle]], the sun does not set on some summer days and does not rise on some winter days.

Constituent part of the [[United Kingdom]] in the northeast of the island of Ireland, sharing an open border with the [[Republic of Ireland]]. Its population at the 2021 census was 1,903,175, about 3% of the UK total. Northern Ireland was created in 1921, when Ireland was partitioned, to give devolved government to six northeastern counties with a unionist majority. A conflict known as the [[The Troubles|Troubles]] involved republican and loyalist paramilitaries and state forces from the late 1960s and claimed more than 3,500 lives. The 1998 [[Good Friday Agreement]] established a power-sharing assembly and advanced the peace process, although sectarianism and sporadic violence persist. The economy, the most industrialized in Ireland at partition, has grown significantly since the late 1990s. Unemployment peaked at 17.2% in 1986 and was below 10% by the 2010s.

Commonwealth and unincorporated territory of the [[United States]], consisting of the 14 northern islands of the [[Mariana Islands]] in the western [[Pacific Ocean]]. The southernmost island, [[Guam]], is a separate U.S. territory. The population was 47,329 in 2020, mostly on Saipan, Tinian and Rota. The islands were settled around 1500 BC and claimed by Spain in 1521. Germany acquired them in 1899, and after World War I they were a Japanese mandate under the [[League of Nations]]. The Battle of Saipan in 1944 ended Japanese control. After the war the islands were a United Nations trust territory under American administration, and they became a U.S. commonwealth in 1986, with residents gaining U.S. citizenship.

Internal territory of [[Australia]] in the central-northern part of the continent, bordering [[Western Australia]], [[South Australia]] and [[Queensland]]. It covers 1,347,791 sq km (520,385 sq mi), the third-largest Australian federal division, but had only 260,400 residents in March 2025. About 52.6% of them live in the capital, Darwin. Mining and petroleum are the main economic activities. Humans have lived in the region for more than 60,000 years, and Makassan traders had long dealt with its Indigenous peoples. A British settlement at Port Darwin succeeded in 1869 after three earlier attempts failed. [[Uluru]] is one of its best-known natural landmarks.

Period of political division in Chinese history, from 420 to 589 AD, following the [[Sixteen Kingdoms]] and the Eastern Jin dynasty. It is sometimes considered the latter part of the Six Dynasties (220–589 AD). Civil war and political chaos were common, but the era also saw advances in technology, arts and culture. The stirrup, invented during the earlier [[Jin dynasty (266–420)|Jin dynasty]], helped spur the development of heavy cavalry. The spread of [[Buddhism]] and [[Taoism]] accelerated, and large numbers of [[Han Chinese]] migrated south of the [[Yangtze]]. Historians note advances in medicine, astronomy, mathematics and cartography. The period ended when Emperor Wen of the [[Sui dynasty]] unified China proper in 589 AD.

Carnivorous freshwater fish, *Esox lucius*, of the genus *Esox*, found in fresh waters across the [[Northern Hemisphere]] and also known as jack or pike. Its average length is 40–55 cm (16–22 in), but individuals reach 150 cm (59 in) and 28.4 kg (63 lb). A 25 kg (55 lb) fish caught in Germany in 1986 is recognized as the all-tackle world record. Northern pike grow larger in Eurasia than in [[North America]], and in coastal regions than inland. The olive-green fish has light, bar-like flank spots. It can hybridize with the muskellunge, and the [[Hybrid (biology)|hybrid]] males are sterile. Anglers value the species for its aggressive strikes and fighting ability.
